issue.title: chezmoi clipboard SIGINT test inherits an ignored signal and fails CI
issue.description: CI run https://github.com/bbugyi200/dotfiles/actions/runs/46047534127 on 662569a34eb9209baa03e4cc50d32356ee2c7a08 passed lint and all repaired poseidon cases, but ssh_clip_doctor_test.sh::test_sigint_restores_once_and_stops_writes expected exit 130 and got 0. Prior CI run 45910998866 on d4cb694cc250b35f6b222ab8ad49f895d9c35463 has the same failure; r8 changes neither this test nor executable_ssh_clip_doctor. Local bashunit 0.36 passes normally, but launching that same focused test after Python signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.SIG_IGN) reproduces exactly. CI installs bashunit 0.53.0; inherited SIGINT disposition is a demonstrated cause, but its precise CI entry point still needs confirmation. In tests/bash/ssh_clip_doctor_test.sh run_doctor starts bash directly; Bash cannot restore a signal ignored at entry. Isolate the child signal disposition explicitly at the test boundary; preserve all clipboard restoration and no-more-writes assertions. Verify both ordinary and inherited-ignored focused tests, full just test-bash, and exact-SHA CI. No production clipboard-policy change without evidence.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Two successive CI SHAs fail identically. Local ordinary execution passes, but the same unchanged tree deterministically fails with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN; this is environment-sensitive signal handling rather than timing noise.

issue.creation_reason: Found by bob-cli-r8.land while checking the exact chezmoi phase SHA. The same failure predates r8, so it needs its own task instead of reopening the poseidon fix.

payload.description: The corrected poseidon tests pass; this independent pre-existing signal failure is the remaining red test in the same CI run

payload.entry: Fixed tests/bash/ssh_clip_doctor_test.sh::run_doctor to reset inherited SIGINT to SIG_DFL via the system Python exec wrapper before launching Bash. Verified focused test normally and from a parent with SIGINT=SIG_IGN, all 32 clipboard tests, and just test-bash (635 tests, 3141 assertions); git diff --check passes.
